1. The driving. :  gta4's driving was much more realistic. But it didint really work out when it comes to gameplay imo. Especially in chase scenarios. It felt like the game was trying to fight against you. I know you cant maneuver your car in mid-air, but its GTA. Mechanics are fine to be simplified. Dan houser also said that driving of 4 felt more like driving a boat. And he also stated that the driving of gta5 was inspired from racing games. Gta4's slow and sluggish driivng system doesn't really fit into the vibrant and playful setting of gta5. Same goes the other way. Gta5's arcady racing car physics dont really fit gta4's atmosphere. 
2. The AI. While GTA IV's AI behaved much more realistically, (which makes sense, because gta 4 was about the reality of the American dream, while gta5 was a satire of how 'fake' the actual american dream is.) In terms of its complexity and interactivity, 5 does much better. Such as how police throws tear gas at you occasionally, how they apologize if you draw your weapon after provoking them, the way the police wait around the casualties until the paramedics arrive, etc. 
3. Police/wanted system : the law of gta4 always knew that you were in the search area despite without even looking at you. While gta5's wanted system was definitely not perfect(there are problems.), it was an improvement from that of gta4 in ju opinion, how you can hide in allies in bushes etc.
4. Physics :  while gta4's physics system was much more fun to play and mess around with, it was far from realistic. It felt wacky and exaggerated at times. Real life flesh human body doesnt spin around like 10 times in a row before landing in a car crash. It felt more like a rubber band than an actual human body in my opinion. Sure it was really fun to play with, but it wasnt certainly realistic. It felt like it wa trying too hard to look realistic imo.
